scenes.scene: A summer orchard on a country estate. A shallow stone irrigation ditch runs between fruit trees. Two children crouch at the water: a boy of about 14 pushing a home-made wooden toy boat with a twig, and his sister of about 8 kneeling beside a second boat she is carefully repairing with string. Fallen fruit, dappled shade.
scenes.cast: young Edmund (14, dark swept hair, strong brows, plain summer shirt) and young Eleanor (8, dark hair, same brows, serious face, simple dress). Children, not chibi.
scenes.light: warm late-afternoon sunlight through leaves, warm gold rim light on both children.
scenes.mood: a lost, happy ordinary afternoon; gentle, nostalgic.

scenes.scene: A white-stone palace dining hall after the queen's funeral. A long table, one high-backed chair at its end left empty with a folded shawl on it. The king sits at the other end, upright and grey. The son (19) stands by the window in naval uniform; the daughter (13) sits halfway down the table, a ledger notebook in front of her.
scenes.cast: King Aldric, Edmund at 19 (living, naval officer), Eleanor at 13.
scenes.light: pale cold daylight from tall windows, long flat shadows.
scenes.mood: grief kept formal; a family that does not speak.

scenes.scene: A private chamber at night during a great winter. Snow presses against a frosted window. The king, younger, signs a document by a single candle while the archbishop, younger, stands at his shoulder holding the seal. On the desk a small sealed brass device glows faintly cyan.
scenes.cast: King Aldric about 15 years younger, Archbishop Anselm about 15 years younger.
scenes.light: one candle, warm, against cold blue snow-light from the window; the cyan glow from the device on the desk.
scenes.mood: a reasonable-looking decision that is the beginning of something terrible.

scenes.scene: The flagship's deck in a storm during the ambush in Bellgrave Bay. Burning transports behind, enemy hulls closing in. The living prince holds the intact royal crown banner upright against the wind; the captain of the guard shields him; a young bugler, still alive, braces against the mast and sounds a call. A lifeboat is being lowered and the prince is refusing it with one raised hand.
scenes.cast: Edmund living (intact crown, intact purple cape, ivory-gold armour), Bernard living (unhelmeted, grizzled 49-year-old, steel armour), Pip living (19, sailor jacket, rust-red neckerchief, healthy face).
scenes.light: fire-orange from the burning ships behind and cold lightning; gold rim on the prince.
scenes.mood: courage at the moment everything is lost.

scenes.scene: The young queen at a large desk in a sunlit study, a repaired wooden toy boat beside her inkwell. In front of her lies a sealed petition with a black ribbon, unopened. The chancellor stands behind her chair, one hand resting lightly on the desk next to the petition, as if guiding her.
scenes.light: bright white artificial daylight through the window, too even, slightly unnatural.

scenes.scene: A palace parade ground after victory. The undead prince faces his assembled undead company in ranks. In front stand his four officers: the captain at attention, the surgeon with arms folded, the lich-scholar holding his slate, the young bugler with his bugle lowered. Some soldiers in the ranks look up at him, some look away toward the sea.
scenes.cast: Edmund undead, Bernard, Matilda, Oswin, Pip, and a crowd of undead soldiers.
scenes.light: white palace daylight above, cyan-green soulfire rim on every undead figure.
scenes.mood: the question nobody has asked aloud: what happens now.

scenes.scene: A small wooden ferry boat on a vast black calm sea at night. The faceless Ferryman stands at the stern with his oar. A lantern hangs from a pole, its cyan-green light falling on one empty seat at the bow. Nothing else in the frame but distant fog.
scenes.light: the single lantern; everything else almost black.

scenes.scene: A formal royal family portrait painted as if hanging in the palace, but in the game's ink style: the king seated, the queen mother standing with a hand on his shoulder, the son at 18 standing straight in a new naval uniform, the daughter at 12 holding a toy boat she was told to put down. A gold eight-rayed sun on the wall behind.
scenes.cast: King Aldric, Queen Beatrice, Edmund at 18 (living), Eleanor at 12.
scenes.mood: a family as it wanted to be seen; small human details breaking the formality.

endings.scene: Night sea in Bellgrave Bay. The undead company's purple broken-crown banner sinks into black water, a hand of soulfire letting go of the pole. On the horizon, the Ferryman's small lantern boat is already rowing toward the viewer.
endings.light: cold dark blue, one cyan lantern.
endings.mood: defeat, but the oars are already coming.

endings.scene: The throne hall of the white capital. The undead prince sits on the white-and-gold throne wearing his broken crown; rows of undead guards stand motionless on both sides. His sister stands apart at a tall window, back half-turned.
endings.light: hard white artificial daylight; cyan rim on the undead.
endings.mood: victory that feels like a tomb.

endings.scene: A guard room in the palace. The undead prince, crowned, stands at the doorway looking at a long rack of empty armour stands and hooks; only the captain of the guard remains, standing beside him by choice.
endings.light: white daylight from slits; cyan rim.
endings.mood: a crown kept, a company let go.

endings.scene: The queen seated on the throne; the undead prince stands just behind and beside her, a hand on the back of the throne. Courtiers in the foreground bow toward HIM rather than her.
endings.light: white daylight; cyan rim on the prince, gold rim on the queen.

endings.scene: A harbour wall in the white city. The siblings sit side by side on the warm stone eating fruit, the young bugler nearby playing a call toward departing figures walking off down the quay. Behind them the city stays bright though the clocks say it is evening.
endings.light: unchanging white daylight, a faint cyan rim on the undead.
endings.mood: a gentle afternoon that cannot quite end.

endings.scene: The first sunset over the white capital: the sky finally turning orange. On the docks, bound undead soldiers carry grain sacks in lines under the eye of the undead king, who stands on a stair above them, crowned.
endings.light: real orange-red sunset for the first time, long shadows; cyan rim on the undead.
endings.mood: the sun went down, the orders did not.

endings.scene: A plain office at night lit by candles. The undead prince, crowned, signs a winter budget at a desk piled with ledgers; living clerks work around him; through the window the city has ordinary lamplight.

A rocky shore at dusk after the first winter preparations. The queen and her undead brother stand facing each other on the shingle; behind him, a line of undead sentinels along the cliff watching the sea.
endings.light: natural dusk, cool violet, gold rim on the queen, cyan rim on the undead.
endings.mood: a promise of a long watch.

endings.scene: The queen on a palace balcony watching colour drain from the white city walls as the first natural sunset arrives. Below in the courtyard the young bugler raises his bugle to sound dismissal; undead soldiers walk away freely through an open gate toward the sea.
endings.light: the first real sunset, warm orange turning to blue.

endings.scene: The last shore. The undead prince steps into the Ferryman's small boat on a calm grey sea at dawn; the Ferryman reaches up toward the lantern to put it out. On the shore behind, his sister and a few volunteer undead watch him go.
endings.light: pale natural dawn; the lantern the last cyan light in the image.
